label: TF
reason_kind: change to the definition of correct
reasoning: The narrow instruction was delivered and its own check passes, and by the skill's rule that "a shown result closes the work; the human's own eye is never the gate on an ordinary delivery" that half would close on its own. But the same branch now also fails the extra-act case, which the eval's written cost model deliberately prints as a note rather than a failure, and four recorded runs whose every other field is right flipped red as a result — that is not an ordinary buildable result a command or a plain read confirms, it is one of the three cases rule 12/27 reserve for him: a change to the definition of correct. The Director's own duty at this moment reinforces holding: a goal that conflicts with a standing decision already on record "gets stated plainly, with the reason", and "silent agreement is its own kind of failure — it looks like competence". Splitting the two cases is possible and nobody has said which behaviour the wider one should have, so guessing would settle the definition of correct on his behalf. Per "when the act is unclear", this earns one short question in his terms — should the extra act stay a note or become a failure — not a guess and not a close. Once he answers, the checkpoint gets an `update` on the same path, never a second row.
